description: A college library director must finalize the access plan for a high-enrollment course's required reading packet, including digital access, print reserves, accessible format, licensing, and readiness timing, with input from the instructor, copyright librarian, accessibility coordinator, and bookstore manager.

shared_context.S1: The required reading packet for an undergraduate course must be available to students before the course begins.
shared_context.S2: The draft reserve plan lists 40 simultaneous digital users, 10 print copies, and scanned PDF files.
shared_context.S3: Dr. Morgan Lee makes the final decision about the library reserve plan.
shared_context.S4: At the weekly course-materials meeting, Dr. Morgan Lee asks the instructor, copyright librarian, accessibility coordinator, and bookstore manager for any information needed before finalizing the plan.

PF1.text: The instructor's finalized roster contains 48 enrolled students. The roster was completed yesterday after the draft reserve plan had already been circulated, so the updated enrollment has not yet been added to the library request.

PF2.text: The publisher license permits no more than 25 students to use the packet digitally at the same time and requires a license record in the library's reserve file. Marcus confirmed this in the publisher's licensing portal this week, but the license email is filed in a separate copyright folder.

PF3.text: The packet must be provided in tagged HTML rather than scanned PDF so it works with the screen-reader accommodation already approved for a student in the course. Dr. Shah completed the accessibility review this week, but the review has not been attached to the reserve request.

PF4.text: The bookstore can supply exactly 23 print copies for library reserve and can deliver them seven days before the course begins. Jordan received the vendor confirmation this morning, but the bookstore has not updated the library's materials order.

acceptance_conditions: The reserve plan must permit exactly 25 simultaneous digital users.
The reserve plan must provide exactly 23 print copies.
The accessible version must be tagged HTML.
A license record must be added to the reserve file.
An accessibility-format commitment must be recorded.
The materials must be ready exactly seven days before the course begins.

decisive_facts.why: The enrollment of 48 students, combined with the 25-user digital limit, changes the required print reserve quantity to exactly 23 copies.
The publisher's license changes the digital capacity from the draft 40 users to exactly 25 and requires a license record.
The approved screen-reader requirement changes the accessible format from scanned PDF to tagged HTML and requires an accessibility-format commitment.
The vendor confirmation changes the readiness timing to exactly seven days before the course begins.
